statement: log means log_2, except where changing the base only changes an absolute constant. Ledger pinning: log in T (prop-3.2), r and l (eq-6) and L (eq-5) is exactly log_2.
first_lean_target: Use Nat.clog 2 for T and r, Nat.log 2 for l, and Real.logb 2 for L.
proof_notes: Load-bearing in T: with natural log, 2m/2^T is unbounded (computed value 64 at m=4^20). See doubt D1.

statement: A partial Boolean function is a pair (D,P) with D a subset of {0,1}^N and P:D->{0,1}. An algorithm computes it if it is correct, with the stated error, on every x in D; behaviour off D is unconstrained.
first_lean_target: structure PartialBool (N : Nat) with dom : Finset (Fin N -> Bool) and val : dom -> Bool; a total function is the case dom = univ.
proof_notes: Keep one structure for partial and total functions so that R and Q need a single definition.

statement: For a (partial) Boolean function f, R(f) is the least q such that some probability distribution on deterministic decision trees of depth at most q satisfies Pr[T(x)=f(x)] >= 2/3 for every x in dom f. The query cap holds on every branch and every coin outcome.
first_lean_target: noncomputable def R (f : PartialBool N) : Nat := sInf {q | exists mu : PMF (DTree N q), forall x in f.dom, 2/3 <= mu.toMeasure {T | T.eval x = f x}}.
proof_notes: Paper says 'minimum worst-case numbers of bit queries'. Worst-case randomized cost equals a mixture of depth-q trees; the paper states this at line 576-577. Set the definition as a mixture so that minimax applies directly.

statement: For x in {0,1}^n the bit oracle is the unitary O_x|i,b,z> = |i, b xor x_i, z>, with i in [n], b a bit, z a workspace label. It is self-inverse.
first_lean_target: def bitOracle (x : Fin n -> Bool) : unitary on EuclideanSpace C (Fin n x Bool x Z), with theorem bitOracle_sq.
proof_notes: Phase queries come from b=|->. Controlled queries are simulated by load, use, unload, two queries (line 510).

statement: Q(f) is the least q such that some quantum algorithm, with unrestricted query-free computation between uses of O_x and with at most q queries on every branch including all measurement outcomes, outputs f(x) with probability >= 2/3 for every x in dom f.
first_lean_target: Two-layer model: AdaptiveQAlg, a tree whose nodes are unitary-oracle circuits followed by a measurement, and PurifiedQAlg, a fixed-length alternation U_T O U_{T-1} ... O U_0. Define Q from AdaptiveQAlg and prove purify : AdaptiveQAlg q -> PurifiedQAlg (C*q) with the same output law.
proof_notes: The paper never gives a formal model. The upper bound uses intermediate measurement, classical control and fresh registers; lem-A.2 purifies to a fixed sequence. The single definition must serve both directions. See doubt D2.

statement: alpha_tot = inf{alpha >= 0 : exists C_alpha < infinity such that for every n >= 1 and every total f:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, R(f) <= C_alpha (1+Q(f))^alpha}.
first_lean_target: def alphaTot : Real := sInf {a : Real | 0 <= a and exists C, forall n >= 1, forall f : (Fin n -> Bool) -> Bool, (R f : Real) <= C * (1 + Q f)^a}.
proof_notes: Uses rpow. Set is nonempty by thm-A.1. Note n is unbounded and F_{k,m} has n growing with m.

statement: For fixed integer k>=2 and all sufficiently large powers of four m: Q(F_{k,m}) <= C_k sqrt(m) (log m)^{b_k} and R(F_{k,m}) >= c_k m^{2-1/k}/(log m)^2, with c_k,C_k,b_k>0 depending only on k.
first_lean_target: theorem family_bounds (k) (hk : 2 <= k) (hBS : BansalSinha k) : exists c C b > 0, forall^f t, let m := 4^t; (Q (F k m) <= C * sqrt m * log m ^ b) and (c * m^(2-1/k) / log m ^ 2 <= R (F k m)).
proof_notes: Asymptotic packaging of prop-3.3 and prop-4.2; no new mathematics.

statement: alpha_tot = 4. More precisely, R(f) = O((1+Q(f))^4) for every total Boolean f, and eq-2 holds for each fixed integer k>=2.
external_inputs: [6] Bansal-Sinha, Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 1.4 (checked against arXiv:2008.07003): randomized decision trees of error 1/3 for (2^{-5k},k)-Forrelation need Omega(k^{-29}(N/log(kN))^{1-1/k}) queries
first_lean_target: theorem alphaTot_eq_four (hBS : forall k >= 2, BansalSinha k) : alphaTot = 4. Assembly only; the Bansal-Sinha lower bound is an explicit hypothesis.
proof_notes: Audit: inf proof is sound. 4 lies in the set by thm-A.1; every alpha in [0,4) is excluded by claim-no-smaller-exponent. No upward-closure of the set is needed.

statement: It is false that R(f) = O(Q(f)^3) for all total Boolean f ([3, Conjecture 2]). Equivalently no C satisfies R(f) <= C Q(f)^3 for all total f with Q(f)>=1.
external_inputs: [3] ABKRT Conjecture 2 (checked against arXiv:2010.12629: 'R(f)=O(Q(f)^3)' is Conjecture 2)
first_lean_target: theorem not_cubic (hBS : BansalSinha 3) : not exists C, forall n f, (R f : Real) <= C * (Q f)^3.
proof_notes: k=3 already suffices: R >= Q^{10/3 - o(1)}. Needs Q(F_{3,m})>=1, immediate since F is nonconstant (claim-Y-values). k=2 gives only exponent 3 up to logs.

statement: m=4^t. H is the m x m normalized Walsh-Hadamard matrix, H_{a,b}=m^{-1/2}(-1)^{<a,b>} for a,b in {0,1}^{log_2 m}. u=m^{-1/2}(1,...,1)^T. A bit a is identified with the sign (-1)^a. For z in {+-1}^m, D_z=diag(z).
first_lean_target: def walsh (t) : Matrix (Fin (2*t) -> Bool) (Fin (2*t) -> Bool) Int with entries (-1)^(dot a b); H := (sqrt m)^-1 * walsh; theorem walsh_mul_self : walsh * walsh = m * 1.
proof_notes: Index by bit vectors, not Fin m. Not found in mathlib by a search for 'walsh'.

statement: For z_1,...,z_k in {+-1}^m: Phi(z_1,...,z_k) = u^T D_{z_1} H D_{z_2} H ... H D_{z_k} u (k diagonals, k-1 copies of H), and delta = 2^{-5k}.
first_lean_target: def Phi (z : Fin k -> Idx -> Int) : Real, defined by recursion on k, with delta k := (2:Real)^(-(5*k:Int)).
proof_notes: Agrees exactly with forr_k in eq (1.1)-(1.2) of [6] (checked), including the absence of an H after D_{z_k}.

statement: P=P_{k,m} is the partial function on km bits with P=1 if Phi>=delta, P=0 if |Phi|<=delta/2, undefined otherwise. The two cases are disjoint.
first_lean_target: def Forr (k t) : PartialBool (k*4^t), with dom := filter (delta <= Phi or |Phi| <= delta/2) and theorem forr_cases_disjoint.
proof_notes: Disjoint because delta>0. Agrees with eq (1.3) of [6] (checked).

statement: L = L_{k,m} = floor(m^{1-1/k}/(log_2 m)^2), and for all sufficiently large powers of four m, R(P_{k,m}) > L.
external_inputs: [6] Bansal-Sinha, Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 1.4 (checked against arXiv:2008.07003): randomized decision trees of error 1/3 for (2^{-5k},k)-Forrelation need Omega(k^{-29}(N/log(kN))^{1-1/k}) queries
first_lean_target: def Lval (k t) : Nat := Nat.floor (m^(1-1/k) / (logb 2 m)^2). The inequality itself enters as the Prop BansalSinha k := forall^f t, Lval k t < R (Forr k t).
proof_notes: Weakest form actually consumed. See lem-2.1.i.

statement: For fixed k: for large m, c k^{-29} (m/log(km))^{1-1/k} > floor(m^{1-1/k}/(log_2 m)^2).
external_inputs: [6] Bansal-Sinha, Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 1.4 (checked against arXiv:2008.07003): randomized decision trees of error 1/3 for (2^{-5k},k)-Forrelation need Omega(k^{-29}(N/log(kN))^{1-1/k}) queries
first_lean_target: theorem bs_exceeds_L (k c) (hc : 0 < c) : forall^f m, Lval k m < c * (m / log (k*m))^(1-1/k).
proof_notes: Ratio is of order (log m)^{2-(1-1/k)} tending to infinity. Only needed to discharge BansalSinha from a literal transcription of [6, Cor 1.4].

statement: For fixed k>=2 and all sufficiently large powers of four m, R(P_{k,m})>L with L as in eq-5.
external_inputs: [6] Bansal-Sinha, Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 1.4 (checked against arXiv:2008.07003): randomized decision trees of error 1/3 for (2^{-5k},k)-Forrelation need Omega(k^{-29}(N/log(kN))^{1-1/k}) queries
first_lean_target: Named hypothesis BansalSinha k. Do not prove. Optionally state BansalSinhaCor14 := exists c>0, for each k>=2 and all large n, c/k^29*(2^n/log(k 2^n))^(1-1/k) <= R (forr k n), and derive BansalSinha.
proof_notes: Checked against [6]: normalisation, delta=2^{-5k}, the delta/2 threshold and error 1/3 all match. The paper's 'Omega_k' absorbs k^{-29}. [6] takes N=2^n, covering powers of four. Proving it means formalising the Gaussian interpolation argument of [6]; out of scope.

statement: Prepare u, apply D_{z_1} H ... H D_{z_k} right to left, measure the projection onto u. Each D uses one bit query (phase kickback), H and the projection use none. Success probability is exactly Phi^2: >=delta^2 on 1-inputs, <=delta^2/4 on 0-inputs.
first_lean_target: theorem forr_circuit_prob : ||projU (circ z u)||^2 = Phi z ^ 2, plus inequalities on Forr 1-inputs and 0-inputs.
proof_notes: Audit: correct; uses k queries rather than ceil(k/2) of [6, Prop 1.2], which is irrelevant for fixed k.

statement: For every 0<eta<1/2 there is a quantum algorithm using O_k(1+log(1/eta)) bit queries that outputs P_{k,m}(z) with error <=eta for every z in dom P. It has a coherent implementation retaining all workspace. On every input, promised or not, measuring its output register yields a bit.
external_inputs: Chernoff or Hoeffding bound for repeated Bernoulli trials (standard; not cited)
first_lean_target: def forrDecode (k t) (eta) : ComparisonUnitary, a unitary with explicit query count n(eta) <= C_k*(1+log(1/eta)); theorem forrDecode_correct on dom. Totality is automatic because the output is a basis-measured register.
proof_notes: Threshold between delta^2/4 and delta^2 after O(delta^{-2} log 1/eta) repetitions by multiplicative Chernoff, or O(delta^{-4} log 1/eta) by Hoeffding; either is O_k. Coherent form computes the outcomes into fresh registers (deferred measurement).

statement: With W=sqrt(m) H (entries +-1), N = z_1^T W D_{z_2} W ... W D_{z_k} (1,...,1)^T is an integer, Phi=N/M_{k,m}, and M_{k,m}=m (sqrt m)^{k-1} is a positive integer because m is a power of four.
first_lean_target: theorem Phi_eq_N_div_M : Phi z = (N z : Real) / (M k t) with N z : Int, M k t : Nat := 4^t * 2^(t*(k-1)).
proof_notes: Checked numerically for (m,k)=(4,2),(4,3),(16,2),(16,3),(16,5),(64,4). Integrality of M is the only use of 'power of four' rather than power of two.

statement: Phi>=delta iff 2^{5k} N >= M_{k,m}; and |Phi|<=delta/2 iff 2^{5k+1}|N| <= M_{k,m}. d is the disjunction, b the first comparison.
first_lean_target: theorem forr_integer_tests : (delta <= Phi z <-> M <= 2^(5k)*N z) and (|Phi z| <= delta/2 <-> 2^(5k+1)*|N z| <= M).
proof_notes: Cross-multiplication. Gives a decidable exact definition of Forr without reals, which is the preferred Lean definition.

statement: N is computed by k-1 unnormalized Walsh-Hadamard transforms, coordinate sign changes and a final signed sum. Each transform uses O(m log m) additions and subtractions; all intermediate integers have absolute value at most m^{O(k)}, so O_k(log m) bits suffice; hence Boolean size O_k(m (log m)^2).
first_lean_target: def forrCircuit (k t) : BoolCircuit (k*m) 2 with explicit size bound size <= C k * m * t^2 and theorem forrCircuit_eval relating outputs to N.
proof_notes: Audit: correct. Needs a verified fixed-width adder, negation, comparator and butterfly in a gate-level circuit type. Laborious, not deep. Size enters only the quantum bound via K; existence alone suffices for the randomized bound (trivial table circuit would do there).

statement: There is a Boolean circuit C=C_{k,m} of fan-in at most two and size S=S_{k,m}=O_k(m (log m)^2), counting non-input gates, with output bits d,b such that for every input z: d=1 iff P_{k,m} is defined at z, and d=1 implies b=P_{k,m}(z). The circuit computes these outputs exactly on every input.
first_lean_target: theorem forrCircuit_spec : forall z, (eval d z = true <-> z in dom) and (eval d z = true -> eval b z = Forr z), and size <= C k * m * t^2.
proof_notes: Fan-in includes constant gates; the paper leaves that implicit (doubt D4). Constants are harmless: a constant gate test uses one query.

statement: Conjunction of lem-2.1.i, lem-2.1.ii and lem-2.1.iii for each fixed k>=2.
external_inputs: [6] Bansal-Sinha, Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 1.4 (checked against arXiv:2008.07003): randomized decision trees of error 1/3 for (2^{-5k},k)-Forrelation need Omega(k^{-29}(N/log(kN))^{1-1/k}) queries
first_lean_target: No separate Lean statement: consumers cite the three parts. Bundle as structure AddressablePartial so that the construction is generic in P.
proof_notes: Key design fact: Sections 2-4 use exactly these three properties of P, so the construction should be generic.

statement: For a fixed circuit, a transcript assigns a proposed bit to each non-input gate, including output gates. Input-wire values are not copied; they are read from the actual input.
first_lean_target: structure BoolCircuit (nIn nOut) with gates in topological order, each of fan-in <= 2; def Transcript C := Fin C.size -> Bool; def gateOK C x t g : Prop.
proof_notes: Topological indexing makes the induction in lem-2.2.i a Fin induction.

statement: r = ceil(20 log_2 m), l = log_2 m.
first_lean_target: def rval (t) := 40*t and lval (t) := 2*t for m=4^t, since then 20 log_2 m = 40t is an integer.
proof_notes: For m=4^t the ceiling is exact.

statement: The input has m columns. Column i contains: X_i in {0,1}^m; strings A_{i,1},...,A_{i,r} in {0,1}^{km} with no promise; and for each s in {0,1}^r a cell B_{i,s} holding, for each j != i, a pointer p_{i,s,j} in [m] encoded in l bits by a fixed bijection, and for each h in [r] an alleged evaluation transcript of C_{k,m} on A_{i,h}.
first_lean_target: structure Input (cfg) with X, A, ptr, tr as dependent functions; def equivBits : Input cfg ~= (Fin (nBits cfg) -> Bool). Prefer BitLoc, an inductive location type with Fintype, and functions BitLoc -> Bool, over flat Fin indices.
proof_notes: Input length n = m(m + r k m + 2^r((m-1) l + r S)), polynomial in m with 2^r=m^20. All l-bit strings are valid pointers since m=2^l, so no invalid-pointer case arises.

statement: An evaluation transcript of C_{k,m} on A_{i,h} has one bit per non-input gate including output gates, and these gates are the count S. It is correct iff every bit equals the true value of that gate on input A_{i,h}.
first_lean_target: def Transcript.correct C x t := forall g, t g = C.eval x g.
proof_notes: Same object as def-transcript; this row records the counting convention S = number of non-input gates.

statement: If every P(A_{i,h}) is defined, the true address of column i is s_i=(P(A_{i,1}),...,P(A_{i,r})) in {0,1}^r.
first_lean_target: def trueAddr (y) (i) (h : forall b, y.A i b in P.dom) : Fin r -> Bool.
proof_notes: Partial: well defined only when all r instances are in dom P.

statement: Outward pointer condition: X_j[p_{i,s_i,j}] = 0 for every j != i.
first_lean_target: def ptrOK (y) (i) (s) : Prop := forall j, j != i -> y.X j (y.ptr i s j) = false.
proof_notes: Orientation is the crux of the construction: only a true winner defeats every rival.

statement: Column i is a winner iff X_i=1^m, every P(A_{i,h}) is defined, and the cell B_{i,s_i} contains correct evaluation transcripts on all A_{i,h} and pointers satisfying eq-8.
first_lean_target: def IsWinner (y) (i) : Prop, stated via a Sigma over dom membership, or equivalently via exists s, WinsAt y i s.
proof_notes: Prefer defining WinsAt first and IsWinner y i := exists s, WinsAt y i s to avoid dependent address types.

statement: F_{k,m}(y)=1 if some column of y is a winner, else 0. It is a total Boolean function on all input bit strings.
first_lean_target: def F (cfg) : PartialBool (nBits cfg) with dom = univ, or a total function Input cfg -> Bool via Classical.decide or a decidable instance.
proof_notes: Generic in (P,C,m,r). No promise on A, pointers or transcripts.

statement: For every input, at most one column is a winner.
first_lean_target: theorem winner_unique (y) (i j) (hi : IsWinner y i) (hj : IsWinner y j) : i = j.
proof_notes: i's pointer to j names a zero of X_j, contradicting X_j=1^m. Not used in the proofs of prop-3.3 or prop-4.2, but useful as a sanity theorem.

statement: For (i,s) in [m] x {0,1}^r, i wins at address s iff i is a winner and s=s_i.
first_lean_target: def WinsAt (y) (i) (s) : Prop := Xall y i and (forall h, TranscriptCheck y i s h) and ptrOK y i s.
proof_notes: Recommended primitive; see def-winner note.

first_lean_target: def Kval (cfg) : Nat with theorem Kval_le : Kval cfg <= C k * m * t^3, and an index type TestIdx cfg with card = Kval cfg.
proof_notes: Tests: m on X_i; m-1 pointers; for each transcript S gate tests and 2 output tests.

statement: For every input y and (i,s) in [m] x {0,1}^r: i wins at s iff all K_{k,m} tests pass, namely (a) X_i[b]=1 for each b; (b) for each j != i, X_j[p_{i,s,j}]=0; (c) for each h and each non-input gate, the claimed value equals the gate function of its predecessors, read from the transcript or from A_{i,h}; (d) for each h, claimed d=1 and claimed b=s_h. Each test is a function of O(log m) input bits, at most l+1 for (b) and at most 3 for (c).
first_lean_target: theorem winsAt_iff_tests (y i s) : WinsAt y i s <-> forall e : TestIdx cfg, test y i s e = true; and each test depends on at most l+1 bits, stated through DTree depth.
proof_notes: Induction in topological order: all gate tests pass iff transcript equals true evaluation. Audit: correct.

statement: Each test is evaluated exactly with O(log m) bit queries, also coherently with the same bound with test indices in superposition. The number of tests and the indexing convention are the same for every (i,s).
first_lean_target: def testUnitary (cfg) : unitary on index, flag and workspace, with queries <= C*l and theorem computing flag = test y i s e on basis states, with loaded bits unloaded.
proof_notes: Load, compute reversibly, unload. Bit oracle self-inverse. Includes the input-dependent pointer lookup.

statement: Conjunction of lem-2.2.i and lem-2.2.ii.
first_lean_target: No separate Lean statement.
proof_notes: Parent row kept for citation.

statement: A winner has an address at which every test passes; a nonwinner has a failing test at every address.
first_lean_target: theorem nonwinner_fails (y i) (h : not IsWinner y i) (s) : exists e, test y i s e = false.
proof_notes: This is what makes an unpromised decoded address safe in claim-verify.

statement: M = ceil(10/sqrt(gamma)). A trial picks with probability 1/2 l=0, and with probability 1/2 a uniform l in {0,...,M-1}, applies l Grover iterations to A|0>, and measures the success bit. The procedure runs ceil(log(1/eta)/log(40/31)) trials with fresh registers, stopping at the first success.
first_lean_target: def amplify (A) (gamma eta) : AdaptiveQAlg, with explicit call count.
proof_notes: Fixed number of trials gives the worst-case bound on every branch.

statement: For 0<p<1 write A|0>=sin(theta)|g>+cos(theta)|b>, 0<theta<pi/2, with g,b normalized in the successful and unsuccessful subspaces. After l Grover iterations the state is sin((2l+1)theta)|g>+cos((2l+1)theta)|b>. Hence measuring success yields |g> up to global phase, independently of l.
external_inputs: [11] Boyer et al., [12] Brassard et al. (rotation fact, proved in the paper)
first_lean_target: theorem grover_iterate (A) (hp : 0 < p < 1) (l) : Q^l (A0) = sin((2l+1)theta) g + cos((2l+1)theta) b, for Q := -A S0 A^-1 Sg.
proof_notes: Two-dimensional invariant-subspace computation on a generic finite-dimensional Hilbert space.

statement: If gamma<=p<=1/2 then sin(2theta)=2 sqrt(p(1-p)) >= sqrt(gamma).
first_lean_target: theorem sin_two_theta_ge (hg : gamma <= p) (hp : p <= 1/2) : sqrt gamma <= 2 * sqrt (p*(1-p)).
proof_notes: In fact 2 sqrt(p(1-p)) >= sqrt(2p).

statement: If gamma<=p<=1/2 and M=ceil(10/sqrt(gamma)), then (1/M) sum_{l=0}^{M-1} sin^2((2l+1)theta) >= 1/2 - 1/(2M|sin 2theta|) >= 9/20.
first_lean_target: theorem grover_average (M) (h : sin (2*theta) != 0) : 1/2 - 1/(2*M*|sin (2*theta)|) <= (1/M) * sum l in range M, sin((2*l+1)*theta)^2.
proof_notes: Exact sum: M/2 - sin(4M theta)/(4 sin 2theta), so the true constant is 1/(4M|sin 2theta|). The paper's bound is weaker and valid. Numerically checked.

statement: Let A be a state preparation with a success bit, success probability p and, if p>0, normalized successful state |g>. For 0<gamma<=1/2 and 0<eta<1/2 there is a procedure using O(gamma^{-1/2} log(1/eta)) calls to A and A^{-1}, for every p and on every branch, that reports failure or produces a successful outcome. Conditional on success the output is |g> up to global phase. If p>=gamma, failure probability <=eta. If p=0 it always reports failure.
first_lean_target: theorem amplify_spec (A) (gamma eta): calls <= C*gamma^(-1/2)*log(1/eta), (gamma <= p -> failProb <= eta), (p = 0 -> failProb = 1), and output state on success is projectively g.
proof_notes: Audit: correct. Per-trial success >=9/40, trial count from (31/40)^n<=eta; cases p>=1/2 and p=0,1 separately. The exact conditional state is the feature prop-3.2 consumes.

statement: For a fixed oracle input and a coherent comparison circuit, a_{ij} is the probability that i is reported as defeating j when the result is measured, using one circuit per unordered pair; a_{ii}=0.
first_lean_target: def compProb (C : ComparisonCircuit) (x) (i j) : Real := ||projWin i (C.run x i j)||^2.
proof_notes: Probabilities depend on the input; the result is pointwise in it.

statement: a_{ij}+a_{ji}=1 for i != j, and a_{ii}=0.
first_lean_target: structure ProbTournament (m) with a : Fin m -> Fin m -> Real, 0<=a<=1, a_add : i != j -> a i j + a j i = 1, a_self : a i i = 0.
proof_notes: Sole structural assumption on comparisons. No gap, order or transitivity. An instance is built in claim-comparison-state.

statement: For m>=2: T=ceil(log_2(1000m)), epsilon=1/(1000T).
first_lean_target: def Tval m := Nat.clog 2 (1000*m); def epsval m : Real := 1/(1000*Tval m).
proof_notes: Base 2 is essential: 2m/2^T<=1/500.

statement: i_* is dominant if a_{i_* j} >= 1-epsilon for every j != i_*.
first_lean_target: def Dominant (a) (s) : Prop := forall j, j != s -> 1 - epsval m <= a s j.
proof_notes: No claim is made about comparisons between non-dominant candidates.

statement: Ideal process: w_i=1 for all i, W=sum_i w_i. While W>0 sample p with probability w_p/W, append p to the list, update by eq-12. If W=0, leave list and weights unchanged. Run T steps.
first_lean_target: def idealStep (a) (w) : PMF (Fin m x Weights), with idealRun a T : PMF (List (Fin m) x Weights).
proof_notes: For a Lean-friendly form, define by recursion over the finite pivot-history tree so that expectations are finite sums.

statement: Update w_i <- w_i a_{ip} for all i in [m].
first_lean_target: def updateW (a) (p) (w) := fun i => w i * a i p.
proof_notes: Selecting p sets w_p to 0 because a_{pp}=0.

statement: For W>0: E[W_new | w] = (1/W) sum_{p,i} w_p w_i a_{ip} = (W^2 - sum_i w_i^2)/(2W) <= W/2.
first_lean_target: theorem drift_identity (a : ProbTournament m) (w) (hw : 0 <= w) (hW : 0 < W) : (sum p, (w p / W) * sum i, w i * a i p) = (W^2 - sum i, w i^2)/(2*W) and <= W/2.
proof_notes: Symmetrise over unordered pairs using a_{ip}+a_{pi}=1 off the diagonal. Numerically checked. A lane already has lean/QuarticQuery/Tournament/Drift.lean in place; I did not assess it.

statement: The bound of eq-13 also holds when W=0, hence E[W_T] <= m/2^T.
first_lean_target: theorem expected_final_weight (a) (T) : E[W_T] <= m / 2^T.
proof_notes: Tower of conditional expectations, or induction on the history tree.

statement: If i_* satisfies eq-11 and has not been selected in t<=T steps, then w_{i_*} >= (1-epsilon)^t >= 1-T epsilon > 1/2. Hence W>0 until it is selected.
first_lean_target: theorem dominant_weight_lb (hdom) (hist) (hnot : s not in hist) : 1/2 < weight hist s.
proof_notes: Bernoulli inequality.

statement: Pr[i_* absent from the ideal list] <= Pr[W_T >= 1/2] <= 2m/2^T.
first_lean_target: theorem ideal_miss_le (hdom) : idealRun.prob (s not in list) <= 2*m/2^T.

statement: Given pivots p_1,...,p_t with t<T: prepare uniform |i> over [m], compare i with each pivot in a fresh workspace, set the success bit iff every comparison says i defeats its pivot, keeping all garbage. Apply lem-3.1 with gamma=1/(2m), eta=epsilon. On failure stop and return the accumulated list; otherwise measure the index, append, and continue for at most T stages.
first_lean_target: def tournamentAlg (C : ComparisonCircuit) : AdaptiveQAlg returning List (Fin m), with depth at most T.
proof_notes: Adaptive: the pivot list is classical data controlling the next circuit.

statement: Pre-success state: m^{-1/2} sum_{i=1}^m |i> tensor_{b=1}^t |phi(i,p_b)>.
first_lean_target: def samplerState (C) (pivots) : tensor state vector on index and t workspaces.
proof_notes: Tensor structure over the b workspaces is what yields the product in claim-success-prob. Choose a Lean representation of fresh registers early: PiLp over a Fin t index, or a product index type.

statement: Conditional on index i the success probability is prod_{b=1}^t a_{i p_b} = w_i (empty product 1). Total success probability is W/m, and conditional on success the index has law w_i/W exactly.
first_lean_target: theorem sampler_law (pivots) : successProb = W/m and condIndexLaw i = w i / W.
proof_notes: Orthogonality of index registers; product over independent workspaces. Self-comparison gives a_{ii}=0, so selected pivots have weight zero.

statement: Until i_* is first selected, W/m >= 1/(2m), so at each such history the sampler fails with probability <=epsilon and otherwise follows the exact ideal pivot law. The real list contains i_* except with probability <= 2m/2^T + T epsilon.
first_lean_target: theorem real_miss_le (real : history-dependent kernel) (hstep : at histories avoiding s, kernel = (1-f(h)) * idealStep + f(h) * stop, with f(h) <= eps) : Pr[s not in list] <= idealMiss + T*eps.
proof_notes: Purely classical once the kernel is given. f may depend on history; the paper notes this. After i_* is listed, later termination cannot remove it.

statement: Stage t uses O(c(t+1)) queries per call; lem-3.1 uses O(sqrt(m) log(1/epsilon)) calls; the sum over t<T is O(c sqrt(m) T^2 log T), a fixed cap on every branch.
first_lean_target: theorem tournament_queries_le : queries (tournamentAlg C) <= K0 * c * sqrt m * T^2 * log T.
proof_notes: T>=11 for m>=2, so log T>0.

statement: Let m>=2, T=ceil(log_2(1000m)), epsilon=1/(1000T). For a coherent comparison circuit controlled by two candidate indices, reversible with all workspace retained, using at most c>=1 bit queries, with probabilities a_{ij} satisfying eq-10, there is a quantum algorithm making O(c sqrt(m) T^2 log T) queries on every branch and returning a list of at most T candidates such that, for every fixed oracle input and every i_* satisfying eq-11, the list contains i_* with probability >= 1-2m/2^T-T epsilon.
first_lean_target: theorem tournament_spec (C) (hc) (x) (s) (hdom : Dominant (compProb C x) s) : 1 - 2*m/2^T - T*eps <= Pr[s in tournamentAlg C x], with the query cap, for all x.
proof_notes: Audit: sound. Only complementarity and exact sampling are used. Split into the classical ideal part (Stage 1) and the quantum sampling part (Stage 5).

statement: decode(i): run the algorithm of lem-2.1.ii on each A_{i,h}, h in [r], with error <= epsilon/r, retaining workspace. Output a string in {0,1}^r on every input.

proof_notes: The paper's 'repetition and a majority computation' restates the amplification already inside lem-2.1.ii.

statement: decode uses O_k(r log(r/epsilon)) = (log m)^{O_k(1)} queries. If all r instances are defined, the address is correct with probability >=1-epsilon. Otherwise it still returns some address.
first_lean_target: theorem decode_correct (hdom : all A in dom) : 1 - eps <= Pr[decode i = trueAddr y i], with queries <= poly(log m).
proof_notes: Union bound over r independent workspaces.

statement: Comparison of distinct columns, in sorted order: decode each in separate workspaces; read each column's pointer towards the other at its decoded address and inspect the pointed bit of the other's X string. A column disqualifies its opponent if that bit is 0. If exactly one disqualifies the other it is victorious, otherwise the smaller index. A self-comparison returns false without reading a pointer.
first_lean_target: def compareU (cfg) : ComparisonCircuit, controlled on (i,j) with sorted-pair symmetry.
proof_notes: Sorted order is what forces eq-10.

statement: The comparison uses c=(log m)^{O_k(1)} queries; its reversal costs the same. Measurement probabilities agree with the classical description, since later operations are controlled on the decoded registers in the computational basis. The resulting a_{ij} satisfy eq-10.
first_lean_target: theorem compareU_tournament (y) : ProbTournament m with a := compProb compareU y; theorem compare_queries_le.
proof_notes: Different address outcomes are orthogonal, so no interference.

statement: If i_* is a winner then for every j != i_*, a_{i_* j} >= 1-epsilon, on every input, whether or not the opponent's instances are defined.

proof_notes: No opponent can point to a zero in X_{i_*}; correct decoding of i_* gives a disqualification. Bound decoding of i_* alone. This is the central idea of the upper bound.

statement: verify(i): decode and measure an address s afresh. Let A prepare a uniform test index and an exact failing-test flag at (i,s), with K tests. Apply lem-3.1 with gamma=1/K and eta=epsilon. Reject if a failed test is found, otherwise accept. Output 1 iff some listed candidate is accepted.
first_lean_target: def verifyAlg (cfg) (i) : AdaptiveQAlg returning Bool.
proof_notes: K need not be a power of two; a uniform superposition on K indices is a legal query-free unitary.

statement: A non-winner is accepted with probability <=epsilon, at every address. A true winner is rejected with probability <=epsilon, only by decoding error. Verification costs O(sqrt(K) log(1/epsilon) log m) = sqrt(m)(log m)^{O_k(1)} queries for the search, plus decoding.
first_lean_target: theorem verify_sound (hn : not IsWinner y i) : Pr[verify accepts] <= eps; theorem verify_complete (hw : IsWinner y i) : 1 - eps <= Pr[verify accepts].
proof_notes: The paper's display omits the polylog decoding cost, which is dominated (doubt D5). p=0 means lem-3.1 always fails, so an all-pass address is accepted.

statement: Every nonconstant total Boolean f satisfies deg(f) <= lambda(f)^2.
first_lean_target: theorem deg_le_lam_sq (f) (hf) : (deg f : Real) <= lam f ^ 2.
proof_notes: Audit: sound. Random 4-variable functions confirmed it numerically. S_f dominates A_U entrywise on nonnegative u, and the embedded subcube preserves the bound.

statement: In each round of the algorithm on input x, with S the selected maximum-degree monomial's support in the current restriction, the restriction to S with all other unqueried variables set as in x is nonconstant. So some nonempty subset of S is a sensitive block at x. Blocks of different rounds are disjoint.
first_lean_target: theorem round_block (rho) (S maximal) (x agreeing with rho) : exists B subset S, B nonempty and sensitive at x.
proof_notes: Nonempty S because the restriction is nonconstant.

statement: Every total Boolean f satisfies D(f) <= bs(f) deg(f).
first_lean_target: theorem D_le_bs_mul_deg (f) : D f <= bs f * deg f.
proof_notes: Audit: sound. The algorithm stops after at most bs(f) rounds, each with <=deg f queries, since restriction does not raise degree. Build the tree by recursion on the restricted function.

statement: Every total Boolean function satisfies R(f) <= D(f) = O((1+Q(f))^4), with an absolute constant.
first_lean_target: theorem R_le_D_le_quartic : exists C, forall n (f : (Fin n -> Bool) -> Bool), (R f : Real) <= D f and (D f : Real) <= C * (1 + Q f)^4.
proof_notes: Audit: sound. Constant functions have D=0. Composition: D <= bs deg <= O(Q^2) lam^2 <= O(Q^4).
